text:
A: Alright, mate? Darren. Can you hear me?
B: Yes, loud and clear. I'm Nikhil. Hello.
A: Hello, Nikhil. Where's that to, then?
B: Thornton Heath. Croydon, South London. And you?
A: Bridgwater, Somerset. I'm stuck in a kitchen with the dog bed, you probably saw that in the photo. What do you do? I had you down as a proper office bloke. Good at all the paperwork.
B: Ha. Paperwork, er, sort of. I'm a CAD technician. I draw the services for buildings, the ductwork, pipes, electrics. Mostly office refurbishments, some flats.
A: Oh, so you're the one who decides where the pipes go and then some poor plumber has to make it work.
B: That's what the plumbers say, yes. But actually my job is to make sure it does work before they get there. If a duct is going straight through a steel beam on my drawing, that's my fault, not theirs.
A: Fair play. See, I'm the other end. Flooring and tiles at a DIY place in Taunton. I get people coming in with no drawing at all. Just, "I want it to look like this," and a photo off Instagram.
B: And then you have to work out what they actually need.
A: Exactly that, mate. Half the time they don't need the dear stuff. I tell them, you don't need the fancy adhesive for a little splashback. Supervisor doesn't love that, but they come back, don't they. They come back and ask for me.
B: That's a good reputation to have. Trust, you know. We have something similar, the site managers ask for my drawings specifically. It's nice.
A: Yeah, it is. Do you do any of it yourself, though? DIY?
B: Let me think. I can fix a bike puncture. I put up some shelves once, and Swati, my wife, still checks they're straight. That's about it.
A: Ha! That's more than some. I've done our bathroom, the kitchen floor, bit of plumbing. Never tidy the shed after, mind. Here, I just did a call with Gemma, she runs a builders' merchants. I started in one, sixteen, in the yard. Small world.
B: Oh, that's nice, you had a lot to talk about then.
A: We did, yeah, dogs mostly. What do you do outside work? Bit of sport?
B: Not much sport. Cycling, I cycle to the station, sometimes all the way into London Bridge if it's dry. Badminton on Thursdays. Cricket, I follow India in the Tests, loosely.
A: Oh, cricket! I'm Somerset, I go up the County Ground once or twice a summer for the T20. Proper night out, that. Few ciders.
B: I've never been to a T20 live. I'm more of a Test person, I like the slow pace. Five days, nothing happens, then suddenly everything happens.
A: Ha, that's my Wednesday skittles, that is. Nothing happens for two hours and then someone knocks the lot down and we're all shouting.
B: Skittles? Like bowling?
A: Sort of, yeah, but in a pub, smaller, older. Very Somerset. We're bottom of the league again, mind. It's more about the pint.
B: It sounds more fun than badminton, honestly. What else is very Somerset? I've never really been, apart from passing through on the train to Cornwall.
A: Carnival, mate. Bridgwater Carnival, November. Massive carts, all lit up, thousands of bulbs, some of them a hundred foot long. I used to help build them with my uncle.
B: Wait, a hundred feet? How do they get them round corners?
A: That's the clever bit! They're on articulated trailers, and the engineering's all done in sheds by blokes in their spare time. You'd love it, actually, all the wiring—
B: Now I really want to see—
